name: Frontotemporal Neurodegeneration with Movement Disorder

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Criteria for Frontotemporal Neurodegeneration with Movement Disorder

criteria.description: Progressive behavioral and personality changes consistent with frontotemporal dysfunction
Presence of extrapyramidal motor symptoms including parkinsonism, dystonia, or chorea
MRI or PET evidence of frontotemporal atrophy or hypometabolism
Identification of pathogenic mutations in genes associated with frontotemporal lobar degeneration (e.g., MAPT, GRN, C9orf72)
Progressive cognitive decline affecting executive function and language

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive behavioral or cognitive impairment plus extrapyramidal movement disorder, supported by neuroimaging or genetic findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other neurodegenerative or secondary causes of movement disorders.

pathognomonic.notes: Marked changes in social conduct and personality

pathognomonic.symptomName: Parkinsonism characterized by bradykinesia and rigidity
pathognomonic.notes: Extrapyramidal motor signs without significant tremor
MRI or PET demonstrating frontotemporal degeneration

common.notes: Severe reduction in voluntary movement and speech
Sustained muscle contractions causing abnormal postures
searchTerms: twisting movements in limbs or face

common.symptomName: Executive dysfunction with impaired planning and judgment
common.notes: Cognitive deficits predominantly in frontal lobe tasks

occasional.symptomName: Mood disturbances including depression or anxiety

occasional.notes: Difficulty swallowing due to bulbar involvement

searchTerms: problems with automatic body functions including low blood pressure when standing
autonomic nervous system dysfunction causing dizziness

laboratory: CSF analysis typically normal or nonspecific
Exclusion of metabolic or infectious causes
imaging: FDG-PET demonstrating hypometabolism in frontal and temporal lobes
genetic: Pathogenic variants in MAPT, GRN, or C9orf72 genes
Family history suggestive of autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant motor symptoms without early behavioral changes
Typical resting tremor and good response to levodopa
Medial temporal lobe atrophy rather than frontotemporal
Cerebellar signs and poor levodopa response

redFlags: Rapidly progressive dementia with early motor symptoms
Early onset behavioral disinhibition with parkinsonism
Family history of frontotemporal dementia or movement disorders
references: Bang J, Spina S, Miller BL. Frontotemporal dementia. Lancet. 2015;386(10004):1672-1682.
Rascovsky K, et al. Sensitivity of revised diagnostic criteria for the behavioural variant of frontotemporal dementia. Brain. 2011;134(9):2456-2477.
Rohrer JD, et al. The heritability and genetics of frontotemporal lobar degeneration. Neurology. 2015;84(13):1348-1356.
